section_job.evidence: The section explains the two inventory types, the three-tier inclusion criteria, the shared classification basis, and the metadata framework without drifting into excluded detail.

audience_decision_value.evidence: The opening explains why the two inventories need a common boundary, giving an executive reader the governance relevance before the criteria.

evidence_payload.evidence: Each substantive unit states the governing element and its function: inclusion criteria establish scope, CDM domains organize items, and metadata supports finding, understanding, and linking them.

causal_logic.evidence: The revision removes the unsupported claim that CDM is the sole inclusion test and instead describes it as the common classification basis after scope is determined.

reader_facing_appropriateness.evidence: No internal locators, drafting commentary, or document-roadmap text appears in the reader-facing prose.

terminology_agency.evidence: คณะที่ปรึกษา is the actor for criteria, classification, and metadata selection; กรมฯ is used correctly in the inclusion criterion; no bare NCAIF or DCCE remains.

source_fidelity.evidence: All approved concepts remain: two inventory types, three inclusion tiers, CDM-based shared classification, and the DGA-standard metadata baseline with climate-specific extensions.

form_readability.evidence: The three-tier criteria are presented as a useful numbered list; the remaining material is divided into short, purpose-specific paragraphs.

altitude.evidence: The section synthesizes at criteria and governance level and omits IPCC exposition, field lists, code lists, item inventories, and data-quality assessment.

headline_conclusion.evidence: The opening conclusion makes the common governance purpose of the two inventories explicit before the supporting criteria.

findings_over_process.evidence: The prose foregrounds the resulting scope and governance structure rather than narrating the consultant's workflow.
